Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Technologies Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Participants are reminded to mute your lines when not speaking to minimize background noise. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield Technologies' results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberShield Technologies had a strong third quarter, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our EdgeSecure platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas: expanding our high-value customer base with ARR over $100K, delivering outsized performance in our core product lines like cloud security and SASE, maintaining robust R&D investment to stay ahead of threats, and operating from a position of strength with clear assumptions supporting our guidance.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Chen: Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $681 million, representing a 42% increase year-over-year. This growth was driven by strong performance across all of our product lines. Our gross margin was 81%, and our operating expenses were $450 million. Net income for the quarter was $120 million, or $0.85 per share.

I'll now dive into our customer momentum, with a particular focus on the number of customers generating over $100K in ARR—a key leading indicator of our enterprise traction and sticky platform adoption in the cybersecurity landscape. This cohort represents our largest and most strategic accounts, typically Fortune 1000 enterprises and mid-market leaders who deploy our integrated Secure Access Service Edge, or SASE, platform, including our AI-powered Next-Gen Firewall, or NGFW, Zero Trust Network Access, or ZTNA, and Cloud Workload Protection modules.

For Q3 FY2024, we ended the quarter with 452 customers contributing over $100K in ARR—up 38% year-over-year from 327 in Q3 FY2023, and 14% sequentially from 397 in Q2. This acceleration reflects not just net new logos, but robust expansions within our land-and-expand model. We added 52 net new $100K+ customers, a 25% YoY increase. Key wins included a top-5 global bank adopting our platform for full SASE convergence—migrating from legacy VPNs and point solutions like Cisco's SecureX—and a leading healthcare provider in the EU, driven by NIS2 Directive compliance needs around supply chain security.

Expansions were even stronger, with 103 existing customers upsold into this tier, contributing over 60% of the sequential growth. Our Net Revenue Retention, or NRR, for the $100K+ cohort hit 128%—well above our 120% company-wide average—fueled by multi-product adoption. For instance, customers expanding from our core Endpoint Detection and Response, or EDR, to our Autonomous Digital Experience Management, or ADEM, and Data Loss Prevention, or DLP, capabilities saw average ACV uplift of 45%.

This cohort now represents 62% of our total ARR, up from 55% a year ago, underscoring our shift toward high-ARR, low-churn enterprise revenue. The weighted average ARR per customer in this group stands at $285K, with top-quartile accounts averaging $1.2M—including several hyperscale deployments exceeding $5M ARR.

Geographic trends highlight our global diversification. North America accounts for 68% of the cohort, or 307 customers, with 42% YoY growth. U.S. federal wins, like our DoD IL5 authorization, drove 20 new logos amid CMMC 2.0 mandates. EMEA surged 55% YoY to 92 customers, propelled by GDPR enforcement and rising ransomware—think Clop and LockBit campaigns. A major German automotive OEM expanded us across their OT/IoT estate post a Log4Shell-like vulnerability scare. APAC was the fastest-growing at 72% YoY to 53 customers, with strong traction in Japan and Australia due to PDPA and APRA regulations. We secured a telco giant in Singapore integrating our platform with AWS Outposts for edge security.

Technical initiatives driving this momentum include our GenAI Threat Exchange, or GATE, engine, launched in Q1, which has reduced mean-time-to-detect by 65% for $100K+ customers, per our latest CSAT surveys. We've also deepened integrations with the Big Three hyperscalers—AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud—enabling seamless zero-trust segmentation for Kubernetes workloads. Our Secure Service Edge, or SSE, Fabric now supports over 1,200 inline integrations, making us the go-to for customers consolidating from fragmented stacks like Zscaler's ZPA or Palo Alto's Prisma Access.

Strategically, we're doubling down on industry vertical specialization. Healthcare and financial services now comprise 40% of this cohort, up from 32% YoY, as we've tailored playbooks for HIPAA OT security and PCI-DSS 4.0 cloud compliance. Our partner ecosystem—with CrowdStrike for XDR co-selling and Okta for identity orchestration—generated 35% of new $100K+ wins. Looking ahead, we expect this metric to grow 30-35% YoY in FY2025, targeting 600+ customers by year-end, as macro tailwinds like the 25% surge in state-sponsored attacks, per Mandiant's M-Trends, and SEC cyber disclosure rules accelerate platform consolidation.

In summary, our $100K+ customer base is the bedrock of our 42% overall ARR growth guidance reaffirmation, with durable economics: 92% gross retention and sub-5% churn. This positions CyberShield as a leader in the $85B+ cybersecurity market, per Gartner’s latest Magic Quadrant for SASE.

Next, I'll turn to the performance of our core product lines, with a focus on Cloud Security and SASE, which together accounted for 68% of our total revenue this quarter, up from 62% a year ago. These segments continue to be the engines of our growth, driven by accelerating cloud migrations, the pervasive shift to zero-trust architectures, and the ongoing evolution of the threat landscape—including a 35% YoY increase in ransomware incidents targeting multi-cloud environments, per our latest threat intelligence report.

Starting with Cloud Security, which includes our Cloud Access Security Broker, or CASB, Cloud Workload Protection Platform, or CWPP, and Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform, or CNAPP, offerings. This segment delivered exceptional results, with quarterly revenue of $178 million, representing 52% year-over-year growth and 28% quarter-over-quarter expansion. ARR in Cloud Security reached $2.1 billion, up 48% YoY, fueled by an NRR rate of 128%—well above industry averages reported by peers like Palo Alto Networks and Prisma Cloud users.

Key drivers include robust demand for our AI-powered Cloud Threat Exchange platform, which integrates behavioral analytics and GenAI-driven anomaly detection to combat sophisticated supply chain attacks, similar to those seen in the SolarWinds breach aftermath. We added 340 net new customers this quarter, including 47 in the Fortune 100, with average ACV climbing 22% to $1.2 million, thanks to multi-year deals bundling CNAPP with our data security posture management, or DSPM, capabilities. Margins expanded to 82% gross, benefiting from our shift to a SaaS-first model and optimized data lake architecture on AWS and Azure.

Regionally, North America remains our stronghold at 65% of segment revenue, but we're seeing explosive growth in EMEA, up 67% YoY, propelled by GDPR enforcement and the EU's NIS2 Directive mandating cloud-native security controls. In APAC, revenue surged 75%, driven by partnerships with hyperscalers like Alibaba Cloud and compliance with Singapore's Cybersecurity Act.

Strategically, we've doubled down on innovation with the launch of our Kubernetes-native Zero Trust Pods last month, which provide inline API security and runtime protection for containerized workloads—directly addressing the 40% rise in container exploits reported by MITRE ATT&CK. This positions us ahead of competitors like Wiz and Orca Security in the CNAPP market, where Gartner projects 25% CAGR through 2028.

Moving to SASE, our Secure Access Service Edge portfolio—encompassing ZTNA, Secure Web Gateway, or SWG, Firewall-as-a-Service, or FWaaS, and our flagship EdgeSecure platform. SASE revenue hit $142 million this quarter, a stellar 61% YoY increase and 32% QoQ, pushing segment ARR to $1.4 billion, up 55% YoY. Customer additions totaled 420 net new logos, with NRR at 132%, reflecting strong upsell from our converged SASE + SSE stack.

Performance was supercharged by the hybrid work mandate and the decline of legacy VPNs, which we've seen drop 29% in usage among our enterprise base per internal telemetry. Our EdgeSecure 2.0 update, featuring ML-optimized traffic steering and 5G-ready SD-WAN integration, reduced latency by 40% for global deployments, winning us deals with 12 new Global 2000 customers, including a major telco in the vein of Verizon. ACV averaged $950K, up 18%, with 70% of new bookings being 3-year commitments.

Geographically, APAC led with 72% YoY growth, benefiting from Australia's Essential Eight framework and Japan's cloud sovereignty push, where we've expanded via a joint go-to-market with NTT. Americas grew 58%, while EMEA accelerated 65% amid DORA regulations. Notably, our single-vendor SASE approach is resonating, capturing share from point solutions like Zscaler's ZPA and Cisco's Umbrella, as evidenced by our 15-point gain in the Forrester Wave for SASE.

Cross-segment synergy is a highlight: 45% of Cloud Security customers expanded into SASE, driving a 25% uplift in total platform adoption. Gross margins here held steady at 79%, with efficiencies from our global PoP expansion to 150 points of presence, enhancing peering with Akamai and Cloudflare.

Looking forward, we're guiding to 50-55% YoY growth for both segments in FY24, supported by $250 million in R&D investments, including quantum-resistant encryption for SASE and agentless cloud scanning. We've also announced the acquisition of a boutique DSPM startup to bolster our cloud portfolio, mirroring moves by SentinelOne and Lacework.

In summary, Cloud Security and SASE are not just growing—they're redefining enterprise security in a post-perimeter world.

As we dive deeper into our financials, I'd like to spend some time on one of our most critical line items: R&D investment as a percentage of revenue. In the cybersecurity industry, where threats evolve faster than Moore's Law—think AI-powered polymorphic malware, ransomware-as-a-service proliferation, and nation-state actors leveraging supply chain vulnerabilities like we saw in the SolarWinds breach—sustained innovation isn't optional; it's our moat.

For Q3, our R&D spend totaled $162 million, representing 23.8% of revenue on $681 million in total revenue, up 190 basis points year-over-year from 21.9% in Q3 FY2023. On a trailing twelve-month basis, this equates to $642 million, or 23.1% of TTM revenue of $2.78 billion. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of R&D intensity above 22%, positioning us at the high end of our peer group. For context, while Palo Alto Networks hovered around 18-20% in their last quarter and CrowdStrike at 21-22%, our elevated spend reflects our aggressive push into next-gen capabilities amid a market where global cybersecurity spending is projected to hit $212 billion in 2024 per Gartner, but with commoditization pressures in legacy endpoint solutions squeezing margins.

Core platform evolution accounted for 42% of our R&D dollars—about $68 million in Q3—going into enhancing our Nexus XDR platform, our extended detection and response engine. We're doubling down on AI/ML integration, specifically generative adversarial networks for synthetic threat simulation and auto-remediation. This builds on our Falcon-like autonomous response engine, which reduced mean time to respond for customers by 65% in beta tests. We've also allocated $25 million to zero-trust architecture advancements, including micro-segmentation for multi-cloud environments, directly addressing the 30% YoY surge in cloud misconfiguration exploits reported by Mandiant's M-Trends.

Emerging threat vectors took 28% of spend, or $45 million, targeted at quantum-resistant cryptography and post-quantum algorithms. With NIST's recent standardization of CRYSTALS-Kyber and Dilithium, we're embedding these into our VPN and SASE offerings ahead of the curve—unlike some peers still patching in hybrid classical-quantum modes. Additionally, $18 million flowed into supply chain risk management tools, inspired by CISA's SBOM mandates, with ML-driven bill-of-materials analysis to preempt Log4Shell-style vulnerabilities.

Regionally, our investments are tailored to threat landscapes. In North America, which drove 52% of Q3 revenue, 55% of R&D, or $89 million, focused on enterprise-scale EDR/XDR for Fortune 500s, including integrations with Microsoft Azure Sentinel and AWS Security Hub. EMEA, at 28% of revenue, saw heightened spend on 18% of total R&D, or $29 million, for GDPR/NIS2 compliance modules and ransomware defense—think immutable backups and AI-orchestrated decoy networks—amid a 40% regional spike in LockBit attacks per Sophos data. APAC, our fastest-growing region at 20% of revenue and 27% YoY growth, absorbed 27% of R&D, or $44 million, prioritizing state-sponsored APT defenses like those from Lazarus Group, with custom behavioral analytics for OT/IoT in critical infrastructure, partnering with telcos in Japan and Australia.

Strategically, this R&D intensity is about optionality in a consolidating market. We've filed 47 new patents YTD, up from 32 last year, covering autonomous threat hunting and federated learning for privacy-preserving analytics. Talent-wise, we've grown our R&D headcount by 18% to 1,450 engineers, with key hires from Check Point and Darktrace hubs in Israel and Tel Aviv—our 'Cyber Valley' outpost now at 220 heads. This fuels a 3.5x ROI on R&D over three years, evident in our 92% gross retention and 128% NRR, as innovations like our Nexus AI Shield have driven 25% ACV uplift in upsells.

Looking forward, we expect R&D as a percentage of revenue to stabilize at 23-25% in FY2025, with $750-800 million total spend, ramping investments in edge computing security for 5G/6G and regulatory tech for evolving frameworks like the EU's DORA. This isn't spend for spend's sake—it's calibrated to deliver 15-20% organic ARR growth while expanding TAM from $75 billion in endpoint/cloud security to $150 billion including SASE and identity by 2027, per IDC.

We're proud of this discipline, which has widened our free cash flow margins to 32% despite the intensity.

Before we open the line for Q&A, let me spend a few minutes walking through the key assumptions underpinning our FY25 guidance, which calls for revenue of $5.45 billion to $5.55 billion—a 26% to 28% year-over-year growth at the midpoint—and adjusted non-GAAP operating margins expanding to 32% to 34%. These projections are grounded in a disciplined view of the cybersecurity landscape, informed by our Q4 bookings momentum, customer cohort analysis, and forward indicators like our 145% dollar-based net expansion rate in the quarter.

At a high level, we're assuming sustained secular tailwinds in the $215 billion global cybersecurity market, which Gartner projects to grow at a 13.5% CAGR through 2028, driven by escalating threats and regulatory pressures. Ransomware incidents rose 37% YoY per our threat intelligence from the CyberShield Threat Exchange platform—mirroring Chainalysis data—and we've seen a 22% uptick in supply chain attacks akin to the SolarWinds breach. Enterprises are responding with accelerated zero-trust architectures, with 68% of our top 1,000 customers now deploying our integrated SASE stack, up from 52% a year ago.

Our guidance embeds 27% ARR growth to approximately $5.2 billion, fueled by a balanced mix across our three engines: Cloud Security at 45% of ARR, Endpoint and Workload Protection at 35%, and Network Security at 20%.

For Cloud Security, we expect 35% to 38% YoY growth, assuming continued hyperscaler migration and multi-cloud adoption. AWS Outposts and Azure Arc deployments have driven an 18% increase in average contract value for our CNAPP. We're baking in 40% attach rates for our AI-powered Cloud Workload Protection module, which uses generative AI for runtime anomaly detection, reducing MTTR by 65% in beta trials. This aligns with the 42% CAGR IDC forecasts for the CNAPP market through 2027.

Endpoint and Workload Protection should see 25% growth, predicated on our next-gen EDR platform capturing share in the $12 billion EDR market. We assume win rates hold at 36% against incumbents like CrowdStrike and Microsoft Defender, supported by our 98.7% detection efficacy in MITRE ATT&CK evaluations. Key here is 15% ACV expansion from upsells to our Autonomous Threat Hunting module, leveraging ML models trained on 50 billion daily events.

Network Security is set for 20% growth, with firewalls transitioning to cloud-delivered models. We're assuming 12% net new firewall subscriptions from SD-WAN convergence, bolstered by our Strata Cloud Manager platform.

Overall, we project 28% new ARR from net new logos, 45% from expansions and renewals—driven by our 142% NRR—and 27% from multi-product adoption. Churn remains below 4%, with expansion cohort analysis showing Fortune 500 customers averaging 2.8 products per account, up from 2.3.

Geographically, we assume a stable mix: U.S. at 52% of revenue with 25% growth, EMEA 26% with 32% growth, APAC 18% with 35% growth, and Rest of World 4% with 28% growth. EMEA has strong momentum from NIS2 Directive compliance, with 45% YoY bookings growth in Q4. We're assuming DBNER of 155% as customers bundle our Zero Trust Exchange with data loss prevention for GDPR fines avoidance—post Schrems II, 72% of EU prospects cite sovereignty controls as a must-have.

APAC is our highest growth area, assuming 40% YoY from PDPA in Singapore and India's DPDP Act. China revenue grows 25% via our Shanghai joint venture, focusing on localized threat intel for state-sponsored APTs. Japan enterprise deals, like our recent win with a top-tier keiretsu, embed 20% ACV uplift from OT security for manufacturing ICS.

U.S. growth is steady at 24%, tempered by election-year budget scrutiny, but offset by federal wins under CMMC 2.0—our DoD-approved FedRAMP High solutions pipeline is up 60% QoQ.

Sales productivity assumes rep attainment at 105% to 110%, with 1,200 field reps and a 4:1 leverage ratio on our 300 quota carriers. We're not assuming macro deterioration; IT security budgets as a percentage of IT spend hold at 13.5% per Deloitte, versus historical 11%.

Gross margins expand 150 basis points to 81.5%, driven by 25% scale in our cloud infrastructure—AWS and OCI costs down 18% via reserved instances—and a shift to consumption-based pricing, now 22% of ARR. OpEx grows 22% YoY, or 75% of revenue, with R&D at 18% for $1.1 billion in AI initiatives like our Quantum-Resistant Crypto suite to counter harvest-now-decrypt-later risks from nation-states. Sales & Marketing at 32%, reflecting $200 million in partner incentives with MSSPs like Accenture and Deloitte, targeting 35% indirect channel mix.

Strategically, we're assuming two tuck-in M&As similar to our Q3 acquisition of a SSE startup, adding $50 million in ARR at 8x multiples. Partnerships deepen—e.g., our co-sell motion with Snowflake for DSPM ramps to 15% of cloud bookings.

Risks we're monitoring include potential 5-10% IT budget cuts if U.S. GDP growth slips below 2%; competitive intensity, with Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange gaining traction—we counter with 20% faster inline inspection; regulatory headwinds like SEC cyber disclosure rules delaying deals by 30 days; and geopolitical flares, e.g., U.S.-China tensions impacting 8% of APAC pipeline.

That said, our $4.2 billion RPO—up 32% YoY, with 85% current—gives us high conviction. 92% of Q4 bookings closed within guidance, and pipeline coverage is 4.2x. We're well-positioned to outperform in this must-have market.

We are confident that we are well-positioned to continue to drive growth and profitability in the years to come. Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. To ask a question, press star then one on your telephone keypad. We'll pause momentarily to assemble the queue. First question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith: Thanks, and congrats on a solid quarter. Mike, you highlighted the $100K+ ARR cohort growth—can you give more color on how expansions are tracking in healthcare and financial services specifically?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, expansions in those verticals have been a standout. Healthcare and financial services now make up 40% of that cohort, up from 32% YoY, as we've honed playbooks for HIPAA OT security and PCI-DSS 4.0 compliance. We've seen 103 upsells into the tier, with NRR at 128%, and partners like CrowdStrike contributing 35% of wins. It's all about multi-product stickiness driving that 45% ACV uplift.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great, thanks. Mike, on the guidance assumptions, how sensitive is the model to further APAC regulatory acceleration, and any updates on China JV performance?

Mike Chen: Hi Lisa, good question. APAC is baked in at 35% growth, with 40% YoY from PDPA and India's DPDP. Our Shanghai JV is pacing for 25% China revenue growth, focused on localized intel against APTs. Sensitivity-wise, an extra 5% regulatory push could add 1-2 points to the midpoint, but we're conservatively modeling current pipeline at 4.2x coverage.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Thanks for taking my question. Dr. Patel, with the R&D emphasis on quantum-resistant crypto and Kubernetes Pods, how are these differentiating us technically against Wiz or Orca in CNAPP?

Dr. Lena Patel: Raj, excellent point. Our Kubernetes-native Zero Trust Pods deliver inline API security and runtime protection, cutting container exploit risks amid that 40% MITRE rise. On quantum, we're ahead with NIST-standard CRYSTALS-Kyber embedded in SASE—peers are hybrid-patching. This, plus 1,200 SSE integrations, gives 20% faster inspection than Zscaler, per internal benchmarks, fueling our CNAPP leadership.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Barclays.

Emily Rodriguez: Congrats team. Alex, on product line cross-sell—45% of Cloud Security going to SASE—what's the outlook for platform adoption as you eye FY25?

Alex Rivera: Thanks Emily. Cross-sell is core to our 142% NRR, with 2.8 products per Fortune 500 account now. We're guiding 50-55% growth for both segments, with 45% of Cloud customers expanding to SASE driving 25% platform uplift. Acquisitions like the DSPM tuck-in and hyperscaler partnerships will push multi-product to 70% of ARR by FY25 end.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
